messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty -> auth-monitor triggered: unusual refresh_token usage pattern (anomaly score 0.89) for Redwood-IDP client app 'web-client-prod'. 3 distinct egress IPs observed within a 2m window, multiple orphaned session creations. Paging on-call and security.
sec-lina: Acknowledged. Triage runbook 3.1. Initial ask: has anyone seen elevated 5xxs or user reports? Any S3/log bucket exfil signs? :eyes:
oncall-eric: I'm on it. Pulling recent auth logs now. Will check session store and active refresh token list.
eng-micah: I'm looking at token exchange traces. Saw repeated refresh_token calls for the same user_id but different user-agent strings. Could be automated replay.
infra-alyssa: Network side — IPs: 18.208.45.12, 34.120.9.77, 3.218.6.99. Geo: mixed (us-east, eu-west). No obvious egress to new S3 endpoints. No abnormal VPC peering changes.
support-julia: No customer tickets yet. I'll prep a short internal blurb for CS and standby for escalation templates.
sec-lina: Quick mitigation plan:
- block suspect IPs at WAF for inbound refresh endpoint (short-term)
- throttle refresh_token exchanges for web-client-prod by 10x
- rotate web-client-prod client_secret (requires short downtime for token reissue)
- revoke refresh tokens issued in last 24h for affected client_id/user cohort if we see confirmed exfil
Please call out if any step will break customer flows.
oncall-eric: Blocking IPs at WAF now (applying 60m rule). Throttling rule applied to /oauth/token for client_id=web-client-prod.
eng-micah: Before rotate: can we capture a small set of refresh_token strings and revoke selectively? We have hits: sample log lines:
```
[auth-proxy] 2026-03-15T14:12:03Z client_id=web-client-prod user_id=U12345 grant_type=refresh_token ua=python-requests/2.28 src=18.208.45.12 token_id=rt-7a3f...
```
If tokens are being exfil'd, revoking all will force reauth for customers — medium impact.
infra-alyssa: Key rotation path: rotate client secret in IdP UI -> update secret in secrets manager -> deploy client secret to oauth-proxy service (rolling restart). Estimated 8-12m service impact on token refresh for active sessions for that client_id.
product-nate: If we rotate, need coordinated comms. Which customers are on web-client-prod? Any high-SLA customers? (cc @support-julia)
support-julia: Pulling list now. Looks like 12 active orgs, 2 are enterprise with SLAs (AcmeCorp, BlueWave). I'll message acct owners with a heads-up template if rotation is required.
sec-lina: Decision: apply WAF block + throttling immediate. Collect evidence for 15m. If anomaly persists, rotate client_secret and schedule forced token refresh with a 5-10 min rolling window and an incident page to support.
oncall-eric: Evidence after 15m: additional refresh attempts from same IPs despite throttling, new UA variants. I recommend rotation.
eng-micah: Agreed. I'll prepare the rotation steps and a small script to revoke only refresh tokens with token_id prefix rt-7a3f and rt-9b2e seen in the last 24h to limit blast radius. If we see more prefixes, escalate to full revoke.
infra-alyssa: Executing rotate in 2 minutes. I'll stage secret in secrets manager, create new secret version, and put oauth-proxy into maintenance-rollout mode. ETA 7m.
incident-bot: Scheduled action: rotate-secret(web-client-prod) by infra-alyssa at 2026-03-15T14:30:00Z.
eng-micah: Revocation script ready. Command:
```
./scripts/revoke_refresh_tokens.sh --client web-client-prod --token-prefixes rt-7a3f,rt-9b2e --dry-run
```
Running dry-run now, will report counts.
eng-micah: Dry-run result: 42 tokens matched across 11 orgs. 2 tokens tied to enterprise orgs (AcmeCorp). Recommend targeted revoke + reach out to those orgs.
support-julia: Notifying AcmeCorp account team now. Draft: "We detected suspicious token activity for the web client. We're rotating client secrets and will ask users to re-auth within ~10 minutes. We're available for support." Will post to #customer-alerts on go-live of rotation.
infra-alyssa: New secret committed, oauth-proxy rotated in canary, healthchecks green, rolling to 5% then 50%.
oncall-eric: After rotation: throttling still in place, WAF block remains. Keep monitoring for failed refresh bursts.
sec-lina: After rotation check: logs show refresh attempts dropping by 98% from suspect IPs. No evidence of downstream s3 exfil. Support: any user-visible errors yet?
support-julia: A handful of failed refreshes from users who were active — opened 3 tickets, CS responding with reauth instructions. No major outage reports.
product-nate: Customer impact: limited. Two enterprise customers reported transient login loops; CS gave workaround. Recommend post-incident follow-up doc and an optional credit if it hits SLA.
eng-micah: Post-mortem action items:
- add detection rule for rapid refresh_token churn per user (sec/eng)
- implement selective revoke UI for tokens (product/eng)
- tighten client secret rotation onboarding checklist (infra/sec)
- add per-client throttling defaults (eng)
Assigning owners.
sec-lina: Filing incident ticket and tagging P1 if additional organizations are affected. Current severity: P2 (suspected token leak, contained, limited customer impact). Will hand off to on-call for follow-up routine checks.
oncall-eric: Handoff accepted. I'll run hourly checks for 6h and update thread. Leaving WAF blocks and throttles in place for now. If anything flares, re-pager.
incident-bot: Incident status changed to "contained" by sec-lina at 2026-03-15T14:45:44Z.
sec-lina: Thanks all. Please add any logs/screenshots to the incident ticket. Support, product, infra: sync up for post-mortem at 1600 UTC. :white_check_mark:
